themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 4 reports this week compared to a 0.4-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks—a 967% increase—suggesting a coordinated campaign or enforcement gap in CD413 that warrants investigation into what's being posted and where.
evidence: Illegal Posting complaints: 4 THIS WEEK vs 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (967% spike, z-score: 7.49)
This represents the most statistically significant spike in the dataset by z-score ranking
Pattern suggests either a localized posting campaign or lapsed code enforcement in specific blocks
reporting_angles: Ground survey: identify hotspots and photograph what's being posted (political, commercial, predatory ads?)
Interview local business owners and residents about frequency and who's responsible
Check with Community Board 413 and local Council member's office on whether illegal posting was a previous complaint topic

themes_detail.label: Street Signs Vanishing
themes_detail.summary: Missing street sign complaints jumped to 6 reports this week versus a 0.8-per-week baseline—a 700% spike with z-score of 4.82—indicating a rapid deterioration of wayfinding infrastructure that could affect residents and emergency response.
evidence: Missing Street Sign complaints: 6 THIS WEEK vs 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 4.82)
Indicates systematic loss of directional signage across the district
Community Board has standing budget request for street reconstruction (DOT), suggesting infrastructure maintenance is chronic concern
reporting_angles: Map which intersections and blocks are missing signs; determine if theft, weather damage, or deferred maintenance is responsible
Interview DOT about response times and whether signage budget is adequately resourced
Talk to senior residents and delivery workers about navigation challenges caused by missing signs

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints rose to 6 reports this week from a 1.2-per-week baseline—a 380% increase with z-score of 3.96—occurring concurrently with a spike in curb condition complaints, suggesting possible source (construction, traffic, emissions).
evidence: Air Quality complaints: 6 THIS WEEK vs 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (380% spike, z-score: 3.96)
Curb Condition spike (9 complaints THIS WEEK vs 1.2 avg) may indicate construction or heavy vehicle traffic as common source
648 building permits filed in last 90 days (437 alterations) suggests ongoing construction activity that could generate dust and emissions
reporting_angles: Interview residents filing air quality complaints about what specific odors/conditions they're experiencing (exhaust, dust, chemical smell?)
Cross-reference with active DOB permits in the neighborhoods where complaints are clustered
Check EPA air quality monitors and NYC Department of Environmental Protection data for corroborating readings this week
Ask Community Board and local Council member if air quality has been a prior complaint

themes_detail.label: Curb Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints spiked to 9 reports this week from a 1.2-per-week baseline—a 620% increase with z-score of 5.97—coinciding with heavy construction activity (648 permits filed in 90 days) and indicating possible impact from vehicle traffic and inadequate street maintenance.
evidence: Curb Condition complaints: 9 THIS WEEK vs 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (620% spike, z-score: 5.97)
Building permits filed in last 90 days: 648 total (437 alterations, 72 new buildings, 15 full demolitions), likely generating debris and vehicle wear on streets
Community Board has standing budget request to 'Reconstruct streets' (DOT), indicating long-standing infrastructure deficit
reporting_angles: Visual survey of major streets and avenues to document curb damage; map whether damage clusters near active construction sites
Interview residents about whether curb damage affects parking, wheelchair accessibility, or stroller use
Contact DOT about curb repair backlog and whether they're prioritizing areas with active construction

themes_detail.label: Asbestos Detection Spike
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints spiked to 3 reports 2 weeks ago from a 0.4-per-week baseline—a 700% increase with z-score of 5.42—and warrant urgent investigation given the health hazard, particularly in relation to the 648 building permits (including 15 demolitions) filed in the district over the past 90 days.
evidence: Asbestos complaints: 3 reported 2 WEEKS AGO vs 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
15 full demolitions filed in last 90 days—these are highest-risk scenarios for uncontrolled asbestos exposure
437 alterations filed in same period, many potentially involving building envelope work where asbestos is common in older Queens housing
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings generated the 3 asbestos complaints; determine if demolitions or major renovations were occurring without proper containment
Interview residents and neighbors about health symptoms (respiratory, asbestos-related disease risk factors)
Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection and DOB about enforcement of asbestos removal protocols during renovation and demolition work
Research whether any of the demolition or alteration permits involved buildings constructed before 1980 (peak asbestos use)
